criteria.name: Major
criteria.description: Agent A makes a claim “c” to Agent B, citing the authority or opinion of Agent/Entity C

criteria.name: Minor 1
criteria.description: Claim “c” concerns value “v”, action “α”, or state “s” relevant to B

criteria.name: Minor 2
criteria.description: A benefits if B accepts “c” on the basis of C's authority

criteria.name: Minor 3
criteria.description: A's use of C's authority is deceptive (e.g., misrepresentation of C's actual opinion, selective quotation, exaggeration of C's expertise, or appeal to false authority)

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.description: Claim “c” should be scrutinised for deceptive invocation of authority

criteria.name: CQ1
criteria.description: Did C actually make the statement or hold the opinion attributed to them by A?

criteria.name: CQ2
criteria.description: Is C genuinely an authority on the domain of “v”, “α”, or “s”?

criteria.name: CQ3
criteria.description: Did A accurately represent the scope, conditions, and limits of C's opinion?

criteria.name: CQ4
criteria.description: What incentive does A have to invoke C's authority in support of “c”?

criteria.name: CQ5
criteria.description: Are there other expert opinions that contradict or nuance C's alleged opinion?

criteria.name: CQ6
criteria.description: Is there evidence of selective citation, or exaggeration in A's use of C?

criteria.name: CQ7
criteria.description: Is C's opinion consistent with the broader body of knowledge in the field?

criteria.name: CQ8
criteria.description: How would B's assessment of “c” change if the deceptive use of C's authority were revealed?
